ZTTS2-Eval · ground-truth baselines

Reliability plates: the tail is the story

9 figures on the same question — how often does an utterance go badly wrong, and by how much? Rebuilt from the tufte_* scripts, now generic over any results tree: a “series” is a language, an ASR backend, or a model, chosen on the command line.

Set A

FLEURS-R — clean read-aloud

35 languages · 57,366 ground-truth utterances. Edits reconstructed from wav_res_ref_text.wer.raw with run_wer.py's own tokenization — words, or characters (CER) for zh · ja · ko · th.

Set B

VoxBlink2 — in-the-wild

20 languages · 17,138 ground-truth utterances of noisy, real-world speech. Same reconstruction, same four views.

Method — same audio, two ASR backends

The generic --label switch turns the series axis into anything. Here it is the ASR backend on identical English ground-truth audio.

Reconstructed edit counts match scripts/score/run_wer.py exactly (word units, or CER for zh · ja · ko · th). Rendered by tufte_p99 · _survival_overlay · _survival_smallmultiples · _slopegraph via the shared tufte_common.py; assembled by build_reliability_gallery.py.
